title: Chain-nested root caller on the BIT native word: ordinary BIT saving 0.00385248 (dependency bound, no overall κ)
body:
**BIT dependency bound only; no overall κ.** The chain-nested root caller of the complex companion #6833 ( n=20, 3 thin queries, 18 local calls, 16 merged idles, no supplier tree) is integral, so it transfers to the retained BIT native word (SHA-256 `51203e7fc75ba10bd3ac3f8e675759f47e13d262bea66b6600d1e515095cad78`) by the same procedure as #6726: specialise `q²=1` so the ordinary normalisations become one, reduce mod two (odd ADD becomes XOR, even ADD disappears, SCALE ±1 becomes the identity).

Result: a 670-event binary caller with 20 independent inputs and 18 native stages; complete invoice of 10,086 productive fields and 53,787 paid jobs, rank-mass surplus 753; raw crossing in (0.0038525393934, 0.0038525393935), against 0.0037667234776 for #6726. Finite admission at tested saving 0.0038525 admits ordinary BIT saving **0.00385248** (previous 0.00376669). The ordinary wrapper is two strict steps 0.00374998 → 0.00385 → 0.00385248 with atom 0.004.

The basis matters: the sites use `x = A + f_i + 2Σf_j`, whose coefficient 2 disappears mod 2, but the basis matrices have determinant ±1, so the identity holds over Z first. A construction with power-of-two pivots yields factors 1/2 and 2 and is rejected; this one uses ±1 pivots only (checked on all 1237 complex events).

Exact checks (400 coefficients each): forward over F2 with stage monomials; forward over Z[q,D]/(q²−1); the retained independent reverse audit; the complex caller replayed over Z[i] with its normalisations. Crossing by the retained interval engine and an independent Decimal engine. Controls reject a missing input or output basis, LOCAL, QUERY, merged idle, normalisation, even ADD, a stray XOR, a shrunk idle, the non-integral basis and a saving above the crossing.

Base: 7c49fe32c55de02c2c873655c804b16e4c3fef0a. Retained inputs are unmodified copies of #6726 at 435bbe91fb28cb1d7a569ca70c6c4e9eb302d486, pinned in `retained/SOURCE-PINS.json`.

Reproduce (CPython 3.12, standard library):
```sh
python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/bit-chain-nested-root
```
Expected: `PASS_BIT_CHAIN_NESTED_ROOT` (normal and `-O`) and `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE`.

Scope: the same five framework assumptions as #6726 (native_all_columns, owned_erasure, compiler, precision_tape, analytic_recovery); the native theorem is unchanged. A complex construction must keep its own κ below this saving; none is claimed here. Using the saving in a package ledger needs the two-step wrapper envelope and atom 0.004.
